data.content_ref: inline:Replace the binary attack relation with a quantitative defeat relation where each attack edge carries a cost, and define the grounded extension as the unique fixed point of a min-cost satisfiability problem: a node is accepted iff all attackers are refuted, and refutation of an attacker requires choosing a set of defeaters whose total cost is below a node-specific budget. This generalizes the closure rule to resource-bounded defense and preserves determinism via the least fixed point over the integer lattice; polynomiality holds for fixed budgets because it reduces to min-cut, and committed roots remain valid because budgets are derived from warrant strength. Criticism: quantitative costs may be hard to elicit and may not correspond to the qualitative nature of warrants.
